{#pguh} # Discussion

{#cule} Camrelizumab-based regimens, such as camrelizumab monotherapy and camrelizumab plus chemotherapy or targeted therapy, achieve acceptable treatment response in esophageal cancer patients ([@w:w20]; [@w:w21]; [@w:w22]; [@w:w23]; [@w:w24]). For example, camrelizumab combined with apatinib and chemotherapy as a first-line treatment achieved ORR and DCR of 80.0% and 96.7%, respectively, in advanced ESCC patients [@w:w25]. Additionally, the ESCORT-1<sup>st</sup> study reported that camrelizumab plus chemotherapy as a first-line treatment achieved an ORR of 72.1% and a DCR of 91.3% in advanced or metastatic ESCC patients [@w:w26]. Moreover, the CAP 02 Re-challenge study indicated that the ORR and DCR were 10.2% and 69.4% in advanced ESCC patients who had a history of immune checkpoint inhibitors [@w:w27]. Overall, the previously reported range of ORR was 10.2%–80.0%, and the range of DCR was 69.4%–96.7% in advanced esophageal cancer patients receiving camrelizumab-based regimens ([@w:w28]; [@w:w29]; [@w:w30]; [@w:w31]; [@w:w32]). In this study, the ORR and DCR were 18.8% and 84.4%, respectively, in advanced esophageal cancer patients. The ORR and DCR identified in this study were within the ranges reported by previous studies ([@w:w33]; [@w:w34]; [@w:w35]; [@w:w36]; [@w:w37]). {#roe9} # Introduction

{#z6ss} Esophageal cancer is a prevalent malignancy accounting for approximately 0.51 million new cases and 0.45 million fatalities in 2022, worldwide . Surgery remains the standard therapy for early-stage esophageal cancer patients, but most esophageal cancer patients are diagnosed at an advanced stage ([@w:w1]; [@w:w2]). Despite the progress in the treatment of advanced esophageal cancer, the prognosis of these patients remains poor ([@w:w3]; [@w:w4]; [@w:w5]; [@w:w6]). Thus, investigating potential treatments is crucial in improving the prognosis of advanced esophageal cancer patients.

{#ubr6} Currently, programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors have emerged as a crucial treatment regimen for advanced esophageal cancer ([@w:w7]; [@w:w8]; [@w:w9]). PD-1 inhibitors exert their effect by inhibiting the interaction between PD-1 and its ligands, which enhances T cell activity, thereby strengthening the capability of the immune system to recognize and eliminate cancer cells [@w:w10]. Previous studies have illustrated that several PD-1 inhibitors, such as nivolumab and pembrolizumab, have exhibited promising efficacy in various malignancies, including esophageal cancer ([@w:w11]; [@w:w12]; [@w:w13]; [@w:w14]; [@w:w15]; [@w:w16]).

ops.markdown: We further examined the independent factors associated with PFS and OS in these patients. (1) A higher ECOG PS score was independently associated with shorter PFS; patients with poorer performance status are less able to tolerate cancer treatments such as immunotherapy-based regimens, which may in turn translate into inferior PFS [@w:w51]. (2) Treatment with camrelizumab plus apatinib, compared with camrelizumab monotherapy, was independently associated with longer PFS. This association may be explained by a synergistic enhancement of anti-tumor immune responses, reflected in an increased ratio of cluster of differentiation (CD)8<sup>+</sup> cytotoxic T cells to forkhead box protein 3<sup>+</sup> Treg cells, greater accumulation of CD20<sup>+</sup> B cells, and a higher T-helper (Th)1/Th2 cytokine ratio, collectively favoring prolonged PFS [@w:w52]. (3) Concomitant disease was independently associated with longer OS, although this observation warrants confirmation in further studies. (4) Advanced TNM stage was independently associated with poorer OS, plausibly because a more advanced stage reflects a greater tumor burden [@w:w53]; consequently, these patients may derive less benefit from camrelizumab-based regimens.
